Subject: Aligning MSA & Order Form: security exhibit operability, tenant scoping, and pen-test window

Hi Alice and team,

Thanks again for the time this morning. Per our call, I wanted to capture the proposed approach on the security exhibit and a suggested operational runbook so we can align legal redlines in the MSA + Order Form without blocking procurement. High-level asks:

- Confirm the SOC 2 scope we will rely on (Type II, infrastructure + platform services). Clearsight noted they need evidence of control mappings for data isolation.
- Agree a pen-test notice window and staging access expectations (we propose a 14-day notice for scheduled tests, ephemeral staging credentials, and a single 48-hour privileged access slot).
- Clarify tenant scoping language: production-data segregation vs. shared staging for test purposes. We recommend limiting any privileged inspection to a customer-specific staging environment; production inspection should be via audit rights + evidence.

Attached are two docs: a first-pass security exhibit redline (word) and a proposed pen-test window spreadsheet. Karthik and Laura are copied — they'll own the legal redlines and evidence cadence proposals respectively. Marcus will coordinate ops for ephemeral staging accounts.

Can you confirm the Clearsight remediation SLA expectation (they asked about 30 days for low-risk findings yesterday) and whether they require on-site interview access during SOC 2 review? If so we can map that into the evidence cadence.

Next steps I propose:
1) Clearsight confirms whether they accept 14-day notice and ephemeral staging.
2) Redwood legal (Karthik) will produce tracked redlines to the MSA exhibit by Thu EOD.
3) Operations (Marcus) will publish a short runbook for evidence handoffs and ephemeral credential lifecycle by next Tuesday.

Thanks —
Naomi

Subject: Re: Aligning MSA & Order Form: security exhibit operability, tenant scoping, and pen-test window

Naomi —

Thanks for the summary and the artifacts. A few quick clarifications from Clearsight:

- SOC 2: We can accept Type II for platform and app controls. We do require a control-mapping spreadsheet that ties our data handling requirements to Redwood's SOC controls (HIPAA-adjacent controls flagged).
- Pen-test: 14-day notice is OK. For high/critical issues we need a 72-hour initial notification to our security lead; otherwise 14 days is fine. On-site interviews are unlikely; remote evidence and screenshots are preferred.
- Tenant scoping: We cannot give production-level read access to test tenants. We can accept ephemeral, customer-scoped staging with a non-production data subset. We also asked about whether Redwood can provide sampling of logs for the inspection rather than full exports.

Procurement notes: we need the MSA exhibit to include explicit language on data retention and evidence retention windows (24 months preferred) and a commitment on audit scheduling slots (we request two 7-day windows across a 12-month period).

I'll review the attachments and get back with any redlines.

Best,
Alice

--

Alice — great, thanks. Quick notes in response so the team can work in parallel:

- Control mapping: Laura, can you produce a mapping doc that highlights SOC controls that meet Clearsight's HIPAA-adjacent asks and call out any gaps? Aim for an initial deliverable (mapping + gap notes) by Wed EOD.
- Pen-test notice and escalation: Karthik, we'll capture the 14-day scheduled notice + 72-hour critical notification in the redline. Also include an explicit clause that high/critical findings require immediate coordination and an agreed remediation plan (30-day target for low-risk as discussed).
- Tenant scoping / logs: Marcus will draft the evidence-handback runbook describing log sampling, redaction rules, and ephemeral cred lifecycle. Marcus — please ensure we specify whether we can provide sanitized log samples vs. aggregated metrics.

If there are legal constraints (e.g., we cannot commit to on-demand production exports) call them out in the redline. Karthik, please identify any MSA clause numbers we should reference for cross-linking.

I'll consolidate and send a single tracked redline to Clearsight by Thu.

Thanks —
Naomi

Team —

Attached are the tracked redlines to the security exhibit (security-exhibit-redline-v1.docx). Key callouts in the redline:

1) Audit rights: I tightened the inspection language to reflect a customer-requested audit (SOC 2 reliance) without giving unfettered direct production access. We propose: a) customer-specified sampling/exports, b) Redwood-facilitated auditor access under NDA, or c) mutually scheduled data exports with redaction.

2) Pen-test access: Drafted a notice-and-escalation flow that captures 14-day scheduled notice + 72-hour critical findings escalation. I added a clause that any privileged access is timeboxed and only via ephemeral credentials with a named ops owner.

3) Evidence retention and scheduling: Added a 24-month evidence retention reference (aligns with Clearsight request) and two 7-day audit windows per 12 months as optional slots (customer to use one or both). We also added language that operational load beyond these windows will be scoped and may incur professional services charges.

4) Control mapping: Left a placeholder and a reference to the Drive link where Laura will publish the SOC-to-Clearsight mapping. We should ensure we don't promise HIPAA compliance in the MSA; instead, call out SOC 2 mappings and provide a statement of alignment.

Next steps:
- Laura: upload initial control-mapping by EOD Wed (I will include the Drive link in the redline).
- Marcus: finish runbook + ephemeral account workflow; I will add a short paragraph pointing to the runbook.
- Naomi: send proposed tracked redline to Clearsight (Alice + Procurement) once Laura uploads the mapping.

If anyone wants to push back on the phrasing for auditor access vs. direct production access, say so now — I tried to preserve negotiation flexibility.

-Karthik
